title: Prove the exact 22-call binary chain retiming threshold (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

A binary depth-six dirty-chain connector first admits a commuting retiming that cannot expose cancelling equal calls at **22 complete calls**, exactly two above the known optimum. This answers Open next question 2 of #4748.

```text
1234656564321234565432
   46 becomes 64
1236456564321234565432
```

Claim type: **scoped construction and proof, with finite certificates**. Both words restore every dirty intermediate and add B6 B5 B4 B3 B2 B1 x to the dirty target for arbitrary compatible maps in characteristic two. Each has a noncommuting blocker between every consecutive equal-call pair, so no sequence of commuting swaps can expose a cancellation. This excludes a redundant inserted cancelling pair.

The upper bound and blocker proof are new. The lower bound cites #4748 at `fc09e5b783989d769e6ae6fffeb7d23b30177c86` for the absence of commuting neighbors in every shortest 20-call word, plus the elementary even-multiplicity constraint. No predecessor verifier is imported or replayed. Yifan Kang's Proposition 3.1 supplies the known path minimum and bridge construction. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Only `research/depth6-chain-retiming/` is added. Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Nick Petalas #4748/#4249/#4263/#4281, Ryanson Jonathan #4418 for separate depth-five residues, Yifan Kang and the Nash et al. construction cited there, and Ross Richardson's #943/#934 connector lineage. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19131105).

## Evidence

Before: #4748 left the extra-call cost of genuine commuting retiming open. After: two explicit commutation-reduced 22-call words and a proof of the exact two-call premium.

Local CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only:

- Direct integer interval coefficients and separate 7-by-7 endpoint products certify both new words.
- 32 enumerated blocker certificates prove that commuting swaps cannot expose a first cancellation.
- All 16,384 binary scalar dirty map/state cases, 1,792 two-coordinate dirty replays, 1,536 exhaustive two-map local-relation comparisons and ten rejection controls pass.
- Both registered warning-strict normal/optimized commands pass. Timed direct runs took 0.099 s and 0.122 s against 120-second limits.
- Registered package replay, five-file exact committed-byte/source-history preflight, committed export integrity, and normal/optimized Git-free isolated export replays pass at `ecd0e3512ea3f108112ea4c127dd4ced2369b7a0`. Receipts are generated from all five package hashes.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/depth6-chain-retiming/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/depth6-chain-retiming/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/depth6-chain-retiming
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/depth6-chain-retiming --check-source-history
```

Expected marker:

```text
PASS_DEPTH6_CHAIN_RETIMING calls=22 extra=2 blockers=32 scalar=16384 matrix=1792 relation=1536 controls=10
```

Any CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the local path. Every registered mathematical check ran locally.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The exact minimum depends on the cited #4748 finite classification; it is not independently re-established here. This is one characteristic, depth and equal-price alphabet, with a fully specified cancellation rule. There is no length-22 census or all-depth theorem. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

No physical consumer, native preparation, routing, dispatch, precision, tape/storage, recursive supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. No Lean, Docker or selected-construction cold replay was run. Bounded Python allocation and diagnostic limits are documented in the README.

The research baseline remains `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`. Canonical main was refreshed to `1f87c3578ae546c8f903f7f4d83dc2e2fb99650b`; priorities, catalogue, family status and selected record were unchanged. Pre-commit overlap covered 426 open PRs and 3,682 Discussion records with complete reported pagination, relevant PR bodies, and targeted main/merged searches. Sparse local-note coverage and unpublished work remain outside that check.

## Open next questions

1. Count all commutation-reduced length-22 schedules and their commuting-equivalence classes, beginning with a bounded near-shortest-path search.
2. Replace the inherited 20-call finite classification with structural chronological constraints.
3. Name a real six-stage consumer and price its complete physical boundary before treating this retiming freedom as recursive savings.

## Related open work

- #4748 studies the same depth-six binary connector at the optimum. It supplies the lower-bound classification; this contribution answers its second open question. Numeric length overlap agrees: the cited bridge has 20 letters, each new witness has 22, and 22-20=2. Its ten-schedule count is credited and not recomputed.
- #1930 studies persistent prefix outputs with unrestored intermediates. Its output contract differs from this restored-intermediate chain; its three-call quantity has no shared numerical value here.

Merged #4600 concerns balanced depth-four row obstructions over general moduli, a different depth and quantity. No overlapping new count is asserted.


### Related open work refresh

Before DONE, this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22T19:16:42Z were refreshed. None of the other six new PRs studies the depth-six connector or its retiming threshold:

- #4770 counts rank-one residue lifts over local algebras. Its target counts do not overlap these chain schedules.
- #4769 proves a one-way corank-one header formula. Header probabilities differ from chain call counts; no shared numerical claim is asserted.
- #4767 proves corank-one negative correlation. Its probability inequality does not overlap this retiming threshold.
- #4766 counts square-zero radical reachability over finite fields. Its algebraic targets and census totals differ from these chain words.
- #4764 gives a cube-zero radical target with right-vector cost three. Its paid-factor alphabet and target differ from this six-stage chain.
- #4763 proves unbounded polynomial right-vector costs. Those factor lengths use a different alphabet and target, with no numerical schedule-count overlap.

The existing #4748 and #1930 relationships and the checked 20/22 length comparison remain as recorded above. No conflicting overlapping number was identified.
